meta.location: The valley by the river Sidon
principles: Terms offered from a position of advantage

world_behind.title: Moroni stops the killing to talk
world_behind.text: Alma 43 ended with the order; verse 1 has both sides withdraw a pace. The whole chapter takes place inside a pause the winning side called.

world_behind.title: His terms are weapons and an oath
world_behind.text: Verse 6 asks for the weapons and a promise not to return. Verse 7 states the alternative plainly, and nothing is hidden about it.

world_behind.title: Zerahemnah refuses the oath on honest grounds
world_behind.text: Verse 8 says they know they would break it, and their children after them. He offers the weapons and declines the promise.

world_behind.title: He credits the armor and not God
world_behind.text: Verse 9 says it was cunning, breastplates, and shields that saved the Nephites. Alma 43 spent four verses on that equipment, so the reader can weigh the claim.

world_behind.title: The scalp is used as a sermon
world_behind.text: Verses 13 and 14 have a soldier raise it on a sword point and preach from it. Mormon gives the man no name and quotes him at length.

world_behind.title: Moroni returns the weapons before demanding the oath
world_behind.text: Verse 10 has him hand back the sword, and verse 11 says he cannot recall his own words. The handover is what lets Zerahemnah attack him.

world_behind.title: The chapter closes the book of Alma's record
world_behind.text: Verse 24 ends the eighteenth year and says the record of Alma written on the plates of Nephi is finished. Alma 45 begins a new source.

words.text: The wooden bar across the necks of draft animals, and so a figure for servitude. The phrase yoke of bondage occurs five times in this record and once in the King James Bible, where Paul tells the Galatians not to be entangled with it again.

The skin of the head with its hair. The word occurs six times in this record, four of them in this chapter, and once in the King James Bible, in a psalm about God wounding the hairy scalp of his enemies. Mormon uses it four times in four verses.

The handle of a sword, where the blade is set. The word occurs three times in this record and never in the King James Bible; Nephi takes Laban's sword by it, and here a sword breaks at it. Both uses turn on a weapon changing hands.
Treated at Mosiah 10:14, where it carries the Lamanite grievance handed down from Laman. Here it is Zerahemnah after losing his scalp, stirring the remainder of his soldiers to fight harder.
Foretold. Mormon applies the word to what the unnamed soldier said over the scalp. The man made a conditional threat and Mormon reports its fulfilment as prophecy.
Counted. Mormon says the dead were not numbered because of the greatness of the number, on both sides. Alma 28 and Alma 30 both use the same admission after large battles.

phrases.term: We do not desire to be men of blood
phrases.text: Moroni's opening line to a surrounded enemy. The phrase occurs once in this record. He states what the Nephites are not before he states any condition.

phrases.term: Ye are angry with us because of our religion
phrases.text: Moroni identifies the cause of the war as religious. He repeats it in verses 3 and 5, and it is the ground of everything he claims about the outcome.

phrases.term: Never will the Lord suffer that we shall be destroyed except we should fall into transgression
phrases.text: The condition attached to Nephite preservation. Moroni states it to an enemy, which puts his own nation under a standard in front of the people he has just beaten.

phrases.term: I command you by all the desires which ye have for life
phrases.text: The oath formula runs through verse 5 and lands here. Moroni swears by faith, religion, worship, church, wives, children, liberty, lands, the word of God, and then by the enemy's own wish to survive.

phrases.term: We will not suffer ourselves to take an oath unto you, which we know that we shall break
phrases.text: Zerahemnah's refusal, and it is a piece of self-knowledge. He will hand over weapons and will not promise what he expects to break, and he says his children would break it too.

phrases.term: It is your breastplates and your shields that have preserved you
phrases.text: The natural explanation, offered by the man who lost. Alma 43 gave the armor in detail, so the record has supplied the evidence for Zerahemnah's reading before he states it.

phrases.term: Now I cannot recall the words which I have spoken
phrases.text: Moroni holds himself to terms he has already offered. He has just returned the weapons, and he treats his own statement as binding even though it now works against him.

phrases.term: Even as this scalp has fallen to the earth
phrases.text: The soldier's sermon over a sword point. It is a conditional, with deliverance of weapons and a covenant of peace as the escape, and verse 15 says many took it.

phrases.term: Their naked skins and their bare heads were exposed to the sharp swords
phrases.text: Mormon gives the mechanism of the slaughter. The armor Alma 43 described from the Nephite side is now described by its absence on the other, and the outcome follows from equipment.

phrases.term: Moroni caused that the work of death should cease again
phrases.text: The second halt in two chapters. Zerahemnah has cried out promising the covenant, and Mormon records the stop, the weapons taken, and the departure into the wilderness.

phrases.term: They did cast their dead into the waters of Sidon
phrases.text: The disposal of the bodies, given in one verse. Mormon says they are buried in the depths of the sea, and then sends the army home in the next line.

verses.label: v. 1–7
verses.title: The terms
verses.text: Both sides withdraw a pace. Moroni says the Nephites are not men of blood and do not want bondage, that the anger against them is religious, and that God has delivered the Lamanites into their hands. He commands them by everything he holds sacred to give up their weapons and covenant not to return, and states what follows if they refuse.

verses.label: v. 8–9
verses.title: The refusal
verses.text: Zerahemnah hands over sword, cimeter, and bow, and declines the oath because he knows he would break it. He denies that God did any of this and credits Nephite cunning, armor, and shields.

verses.label: v. 10–12
verses.title: The weapons returned
verses.text: Moroni hands the weapons back and says the conflict is over, then holds to his own words: no departure without the oath. Zerahemnah keeps his sword, rushes at Moroni, has the blade broken at the hilt and his scalp taken, and withdraws into his men.

verses.label: v. 13–15
verses.title: The soldier's sermon
verses.text: The soldier lifts the scalp on his sword point and tells the army they will fall the same way unless they give up their weapons and covenant peace. Many are struck with fear, throw down their weapons at Moroni's feet, and are let go into the wilderness.

verses.label: v. 16–18
verses.title: The rest fight
verses.text: Zerahemnah stirs the remainder to fight harder. Moroni, angry at the stubbornness, orders the attack. Naked skins and bare heads against sharp swords, and they fall exceedingly fast, as the soldier had said.

verses.label: v. 19–21
verses.title: The second surrender
verses.text: Zerahemnah sees them about to be destroyed and cries out, promising the covenant for himself and his people. Moroni stops the work of death again, takes the weapons, and lets them depart. The dead on both sides are past counting.

verses.label: v. 22–24
verses.title: The close
verses.text: The dead are cast into Sidon and buried in the depths of the sea. The armies go home. The eighteenth year ends, and with it the record of Alma on the plates of Nephi.

chapter.title: The whole chapter happens inside a pause
chapter.text: Moroni stopped the killing in Alma 43:54 and everything here takes place before it resumes. The record spends twenty verses on a negotiation and three on the fighting that follows.

chapter.title: Moroni argues theology to an enemy
chapter.text: Religion is named as the cause in verses 2, 3, and 5, and the Nephite advantage is credited to faith. He is making a case, not just issuing terms.

chapter.title: He puts his own side under the condition
chapter.text: Verse 4 says the Lord will not suffer them to be destroyed except they fall into transgression. Moroni states the limit of his own claim while holding the advantage.

chapter.title: Zerahemnah's refusal is honest
chapter.text: He will not swear what he knows he would break. The record gives a defeated enemy a piece of integrity and does not soften it.

chapter.title: Both explanations of the victory are on the page
chapter.text: Moroni says God; Zerahemnah says armor. Alma 43 described the armor at length, so the reader has the evidence for the second reading and can hold both.

chapter.title: An unnamed soldier gets the chapter's sermon
chapter.text: He raises a scalp and preaches a conditional. Mormon reports the fulfilment in verse 18 with the word prophesied.

chapter.title: Moroni binds himself to his own words
chapter.text: Verse 11 says he cannot recall what he has spoken, after he has already handed the weapons back. His terms hold even when keeping them costs him the negotiation.

chapter.title: The chapter ends a source
chapter.text: Verse 24 closes the record of Alma. Mormon has been abridging one man's writing since Alma 1, and the next chapter begins from something else.

applications.title: State the terms and the alternative plainly
applications.text: Moroni said exactly what he wanted and exactly what would follow otherwise. When you have leverage, say both halves out loud instead of implying the second.

applications.title: Do not promise what you expect to break
applications.text: Zerahemnah refused an oath on the grounds of self-knowledge. When you are asked to commit to something you do not think you will hold, say so instead of agreeing.

applications.title: Hold yourself to what you already said
applications.text: Moroni had given his terms and would not withdraw them when they became inconvenient. Before you make an offer, decide whether you will keep it if the situation changes.

applications.title: Stop when they yield
applications.text: Moroni ended the work of death twice in one chapter. When someone concedes, the useful move is to accept it instead of finishing the point.

questions.text: When I have had someone at a disadvantage, what did I say first?
What condition is attached to the help I expect?
What have I promised that I already knew I would not keep?
What in my life do I credit to preparation that I might owe to something else?
What have I said that I would rather take back, and should not?
What am I stubbornly continuing after it has been decided?
What losses have I stopped counting?
